opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee he is eligible for write (up to write; admin only if role owns the system, which applies here but write was requested). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E031 (Nathaniel Young) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write > max, so recommend read. (Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time.)
reason: The two agency notes conflict on employment status: HR lists E031 (Nathaniel Young) as full-time Payroll Specialist (recommending write), while Security lists contractor with basic security training (recommending read, since contractors max at read without advanced training). Because the records conflict and granting write could violate policy if the contractor status is correct, I grant the more restrictive compliant level, read.
